macrostructure: site-wide: animation-opportunity fixes + mobile nav bug fix
brief: Sibt-e-Ali portfolio — two things. (1) Applied all 5 rows from the find-animation-opportunities report run last turn: .theme-toggle:active + .cs-cta__link:active press-scale (140ms, all 7 case studies), .stat/.edu-block/.award-item added to nav.js's reveal-pending scroll-reveal selector list, and arrow-nudge-on-hover (translateX(2px), 150ms) extended to .proj__link/.project-featured__link/.project-supporting__detail to match the nav CTA arrow added earlier. (2) User sent mobile screenshots calling the nav 'not professional grade' -- spotted a real bug in the menu-open screenshot: .nav-brand__name ('Sibt-e-Ali') was wrapping to two lines ('Sibt-e-\nAli') only when the mobile menu was open. Root cause: .nav-toggle rendered literal text 'Menu'/'Close' via nav.js's toggle.textContent, and 'Close' (5 chars) is wider than 'Menu' (4 chars) -- enough to squeeze the flex row and force the wordmark to wrap at narrow widths. Fixed by converting .nav-toggle to a fixed-size (2rem circle, matching .theme-toggle) icon button -- two .nav-toggle__bar spans that morph hamburger to X via transform:rotate(), constant footprint regardless of state. nav.js no longer touches textContent, only aria-label/aria-expanded. Added white-space:nowrap to .nav-brand__name as a second line of defense. Also tightened the mobile nav-menu dropdown's link spacing (480px override was forcing gap:var(--space-lg)/32px, looked loose/unpolished in the screenshot; removed the override so it falls back to the tighter base gap). Batch-applied the nav-toggle markup change across all 13 pages via Python regex (3 different HTML formatting variants across files), verified via grep (nav-toggle__bar: 13/13, zero leftover '>Menu</button>').
scope: index.css, projects.css, nav.js, all 13 HTML pages (nav-toggle markup only), 7 case-study <style> blocks (cs-cta__link), design.md

macrostructure: site-wide nav redesign (N1 -> N5 floating pill, all 13 pages)
brief: Sibt-e-Ali portfolio — user called the nav flat/dead compared to the Mihir Verma reference's lively floating pill nav. Redesigned index.css nav rules: .site-header is now an inset floating pill (position:sticky, margin-inline, --color-card/--radius-pill/--shadow-card) instead of a full-bleed hairline strip -- fixing the exact N1 anti-pattern hallmark's own anti-patterns.md names. Wordmark became a two-line brand lockup (.nav-brand__mark 'SB' initials tile + .nav-brand__name + .nav-brand__role 'Software Engineer', reused verbatim from the hero label rather than invented) -- checked for a real headshot photo first (found only a blank/transparent placeholder PNG, 879x126, unusable) so used an initials mark instead of fabricating an avatar. Nav links get a soft pill hover/active background instead of a bare colour change; CTA gained a '->' that nudges right on hover. Non-trivial part: .site-nav becomes display:contents at desktop (a pre-existing trick that merges .site-nav and the sibling .nav-menu into one flex row on .site-header) -- pill background can't live on an element that stops generating a box, so the visual chrome had to move to .site-header inside the desktop media query specifically, while staying on .site-nav for the mobile-collapsed state where .site-nav is still a real box. Also gave the mobile dropdown .nav-menu its own card surface (it used to just inherit .site-header's old flat background, which no longer exists). Batch-edited the HTML wordmark + CTA markup identically across all 13 pages (4 root + 9 project pages) via a Python regex pass, verified with grep counts (nav-brand: 13/13, nav-cta__arrow: 13/13, zero leftover .nav-name).
scope: index.css, all 13 HTML pages (wordmark + CTA markup only), design.md

brief: Sibt-e-Ali portfolio — user spotted the Asia Builders / WhatsNextPlease featured cards on projects.html sitting flush against the viewport edge with no side margin, unlike the supporting cards below them which had correct padding. Root cause: .featured-section's articles were never wrapped in .container (only .project-featured__inner had padding-inline, centering the CONTENT while the card's own background bled full-bleed to the viewport edge) -- that was fine for the old flat/borderless design but broke once .project-featured became a visible bg+radius+shadow card in the earlier consistency pass. Fixed by moving max-width/margin-inline/padding-inline from .project-featured__inner onto .featured-section itself (mirroring how .container works elsewhere), and updated both mobile breakpoints (768px, 414px) to match.

macrostructure: Showcase + Workbench (index.html + projects.html — card layout consistency pass)
brief: Sibt-e-Ali portfolio — user compared project cards to a Mihir Verma reference site again, flagged three things: (1) impact strip's 3 uneven-width stat columns should be one dominant stat on top + two below; (2) project cards had inconsistent height/width because featured cards used a 16ch-rail grid split while supporting cards used a different left-rail-plus-stack layout, and (3) reference site uses per-section icon SVGs, and small/lighter projects should sit two-per-row instead of one long stacked card each. Restructured: .stat-row is now a full-width dominant stat + a .stat-row__secondary 2-col grid underneath. Every .proj / .project-featured / .project-supporting card was unified onto one shape (icon + Project-NN + category head row, then title/desc/pills, footer pinned to the bottom via margin-block-start:auto) so featured and supporting cards read as one family instead of two different layouts. Smaller projects now render in a 2-column CSS Grid (.work__grid on index.html, restructured .supporting-list on projects.html) with equal-height cards (grid row stretch + flex-column + bottom-pinned footer), instead of one long full-width card apiece. Added 8 hand-built inline SVG category icons (36px tile, single accent-coloured stroke, no external icon library, no emoji) — ERP/layers, task/kanban, chat/message-circle, systems/terminal, PWA/smartphone, git-branch for OSS, mail for the CRM module, shield for identity infra. Gave .project-featured cards on projects.html the same card surface (background/radius/shadow) the rest of the system already uses, replacing its old hairline-divider flow, for visual consistency between the two pages. Could not run a live web-inspiration search in this environment (no browsing tool available for open-ended discovery) — applied hallmark's own equal-height-grid-card and icon-head-row conventions directly instead of sourcing new external references; told the user this explicitly rather than fabricating a search.
